title: The Scholarship of the band room
premise: Xanthe Okafor, seventeen and de facto parent to his younger siblings, keeps his head down at Meridian High until notes signed by the school's legendary ghost—written in ink that shouldn't exist—start naming him personally, demanding he expose a scholarship fund quietly funneled to the principal's nephew. As Xanthe investigates with his best friend Priya, the ghost turns out to be a former student who died before she could blow the whistle decades ago, and her 'impossible ink' is a ledger she hid in the band room. To honor her, Xanthe must go public days before prom, risking Priya's trust when the trail implicates her father, and ending with the fund restored, the truth aired at prom itself, and Xanthe learning that the family he's protecting includes the people brave enough to stand with him.
about_author: Ivo Okafor is a former high school band room custodian who wrote his first novel on breaks between mopping and tuning pianos. He lives near a school he refuses to name, out of respect for its ghosts.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Between packing lunches and running his brother to practice, Xanthe finds the first ghost-note tucked in his trombone case—addressed to him by name, in ink that shifts color under light. The emotional beat is weary skepticism cracking into curiosity: for once, something at school is asking something of him, not just taking.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Wall
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Priya's POV alternating. Following the notes' clues, they find a hidden ledger in the band room wall documenting a scholarship fund siphoned for decades—now run by the principal for his nephew. Priya hesitates when her father's name appears as a signatory. The beat: the thrill of the hunt souring into the weight of what justice might cost.

chapters.title: What the Ghost Paid
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, climax. The principal discovers them and threatens Xanthe's siblings' enrollment; Priya, torn, goes silent. Xanthe chooses to read the ghost's ledger aloud at the prom assembly, naming every theft including Priya's father's. The beat: terror transfigured into clarity—he'd rather lose the friendship than the truth.

chapters.title: Found, Not Given
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV with Priya's closing letter. The fund is restored under community oversight, the principal resigns, and Priya—having confronted her father herself—meets Xanthe on the band room floor, not with forgiveness asked but with the next note in impossible ink: a thank-you. The beat: found family chosen in the aftermath, not the triumph.
